core_principles.text: Regress athletes to teach proper lunge mechanics before progressing them to weighted walking lunges.
Utilize a wall to achieve an exaggerated plantarflexed rear foot, which helps achieve a 90-degree angle at the back knee and allows the hips to drop straight down.
Use the sternum as a reference point to maintain an elevator-like straight up-and-down movement during the lunge descent rather than an escalator-like diagonal movement.

common_mistakes.text: Keeping the back leg straight while attempting to lower the body during a lunge pushes the body forward.
Allowing the sternum to move forward or backward during the descent indicates movement compensation.

consequences.text: Projecting the body forward during a lunge due to a straight rear leg increases force on the knee joint and causes knee pain.
